title: Time, numbers, prepositions
subtitle: Count to a hundred, tell the time and say where and when

explain.text: Numbers up to twenty are new words. From twenty onward Dutch says the **ones first**, then *en* (and), then the tens: **21 = eenentwintig** (one-and-twenty), **34 = vierendertig**, **99 = negenennegentig**.

Dutch

explain.en: My neighbour is sixty-two years old.

explain.text: After *twee* and *drie* the extra *e* gets two dots to show where the syllable splits: *tweeëntwintig, drieëndertig*. With other numbers there are no dots: *vierendertig*, *vijfenveertig*.
Above 100 you say the hundreds first: *honderdeen* (101), *tweehonderd vijftig* (250), *duizend negenhonderd* (1900). Hundreds and thousands are written as one word, *drieduizend*.

items.explain: After drie the e gets two dots: drieën.

items.en: My mother is fifty years old.
A ticket costs twelve euros.
It costs twenty-five euros.
I am thirty-three years old.

explain.text: Ask: **Hoe laat is het?** Answer: **Het is vijf uur.** For other times Dutch uses **over** (past), **voor** (to), **kwart** (quarter) and **half**. The big surprise is **half**: *half zes* is **5:30**, half way *to* six.

explain.nl: Het is half negen. De les begint om negen uur.
explain.en: It is half past eight. The lesson starts at nine o'clock.

explain.text: Use **om** + the time to say *at*: *Ik sta om zeven uur op*. For timetables (trains, TV) people use the 24-hour clock: *De trein vertrekt om negentien uur dertig*.
5:20 and 5:40 use **half** as the anchor: *tien voor half zes* (ten to half six) and *tien over half zes* (ten past half six). It feels strange at first, but you will get used to it.

explain.nl: Wij eten om kwart over zes.
explain.en: We eat at a quarter past six.

items.explain: half negen = half way to nine = 8:30.

items.nl: De les begint om tien over twee.

items.en: It is a quarter past three.

lessons.title: om, op, in and place words

explain.text: Three little words say *when*: **om** for the clock (*om negen uur*), **op** for days and dates (*op maandag, op 1 mei*), **in** for months, seasons and years (*in juli, in de zomer, in 2024*). Parts of the day use *'s*: *'s ochtends, 's middags, 's avonds, 's nachts* (in the morning, afternoon, evening, at night).

explain.nl: Op maandag werk ik, en in juli ga ik op vakantie.
explain.en: On Monday I work, and in July I go on holiday.

explain.text: Place words say *where* something is. They all take **de / het + noun** after them. Learn them with a picture in your head.
